arxiv-2012-06888.title: Electron and photon reconstruction and identification with the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC
arxiv-2012-06888.description: Abstract The performance is presented of the reconstruction and identification algorithms for electrons and photons with the CMS experiment at the LHC. The reported results are based on proton-proton collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV and recorded in 2016–2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 136 \fbinv .

arxiv-2110-10251.title: Higher Coleman Theory
arxiv-2110-10251.creator: George Boxer, Vincent Pilloni
arxiv-2110-10251.description: Abstract . We develop local cohomology techniques to study the finite slope part of the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties. The local cohomology groups we consider are a generalization of overconvergent modular forms, and they are defined by using a stratification on the Shimura variety obtained from the Bruhat stratification on a flag variety via the Hodge-Tate period map.

arxiv-2201-08332.title: Ground State Magnetic Dipole Moment of 40 Sc
arxiv-2201-08332.creator: Robert Powel, B. Alex Brown, Jason D. Holt, Andrew Klose, Kristian König, Jeremy Lantis, Kei Minamisono, Takayuki Miyagi, Skyy Pineda
arxiv-2201-08332.description: Abstract The hyperfine coupling constants of the proton dripline odd-odd 40 Sc nucleus were deduced from the hyperfine spectrum of the 3 ​ d ​ 4 ​ s 3 ​ D 2 3d4s\,^{3}\text{D}_{2} ↔ \leftrightarrow 3 ​ d ​ 4 ​ p 3 ​ F 3 ∘ 3d4p\,^{3}\text{F}^{\circ}_{3} transition in Sc II, measured by the bunched beam collinear laser spectroscopy

arxiv-2203-15523.title: Heat-type Equations on manifolds with fibered boundaries I: Schauder estimates
arxiv-2203-15523.creator: Bruno Caldeira, Giuseppe Gentile
arxiv-2203-15523.description: Abstract . In this paper we prove parabolic Schauder estimates for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on a manifold M M with fibered boundary and a Φ \Phi -metric g Φ g_{\Phi} . This setting generalizes the asymptotically conical (scattering) spaces and includes special cases of magnetic and gravitational monopoles.

arxiv-2205-14531.title: Fair Division Algorithms for Electricity Distribution
arxiv-2205-14531.creator: Dinesh Kumar Baghel, Vadim E. Levit, Erel Segal-Halevi
arxiv-2205-14531.description: Abstract In many developing countries, the total electricity demand is larger than the limited generation capacity of power stations. Many countries adopt the common practice of routine load shedding — disconnecting entire regions from the power supply — to maintain a balance between demand and supply.

arxiv-2211-15351.title: Testing the effectiveness of saliency-based explainability in NLP using randomized survey-based experiments
arxiv-2211-15351.creator: 1 st Adel Rahimi, 2 nd Shaurya Jain
arxiv-2211-15351.description: Abstract As the applications of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in sensitive areas like Political Profiling, Review of Essays in Education, etc. proliferate, there is a great need for increasing transparency in NLP models to build trust with stakeholders and identify biases.

arxiv-2404-10855.title: Warp Factory: A Numerical Toolkit for the Analysis and Optimization of Warp Drive Geometries
arxiv-2404-10855.creator: Christopher Helmerich and Jared Fuchs, Alexey Bobrick, Brandon Melcher, Luke Sellers, Gianni Martire
arxiv-2404-10855.description: Abstract The last few decades of warp drive research have focused on analytic methods to explore warp solutions to Einstein’s field equations. These analytic solutions tend to favor simple metric forms which are easier to analyze but limit the space of exploration.

arxiv-2405-06721.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks are Radial Basis Function Networks
arxiv-2405-06721.creator: Ziyao Li
arxiv-2405-06721.description: Abstract This short paper is a fast proof-of-concept that the 3-order B-splines used in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) can be well approximated by Gaussian radial basis functions. Doing so leads to FastKAN, a much faster implementation of KAN which is also a radial basis function (RBF) network. Code available at github.com/ZiyaoLi/fast-kan .

arxiv-2410-18889.title: Are LLMs Better than Reported? Detecting Label Errors and Mitigating Their Effect on Model Performance
arxiv-2410-18889.creator: Omer Nahum, Nitay Calderon, Orgad Keller, Idan Szpektor, Roi Reichart
arxiv-2410-18889.description: Abstract NLP benchmarks rely on standardized datasets for training and evaluating models and are crucial for advancing the field. Traditionally, expert annotations ensure high-quality labels; however, the cost of expert annotation does not scale well with the growing demand for larger datasets required by modern models.

arxiv-2507-03291.title: Global Variational Inference Enhanced Robust Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2507-03291.creator: Lingkun Luo, Shiqiang Hu, Liming Chen
arxiv-2507-03291.description: Abstract Deep learning-based domain adaptation (DA) methods have shown strong performance by learning transferable representations. However, their reliance on mini-batch training limits global distribution modeling, leading to unstable alignment and suboptimal generalization. We propose Global Variational Inference Enhanced Domain Adaptation (GVI-DA), a framework that learns continuous, class-conditional global priors via variational inference to enable structure-aware cross-domain alignment.

arxiv-2507-18556.title: Large deviations of ionic currents in dilute electrolytes
arxiv-2507-18556.creator: Jafar Farhadi, David T. Limmer
arxiv-2507-18556.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jafar Farhadi, David T. Limmer. We evaluate the exponentially rare fluctuations of the ionic current for a dilute electrolyte by means of macroscopic fluctuation theory. We consider the fluctuating hydrodynamics of a fluid electrolyte described by a stochastic Poisson-Nernst-Planck equation. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equations that dictate the optimal concentration profiles of ions conditioned on exhibiting a given current, whose form determines the likelihood of that current in the long-time limit.

arxiv-2601-12692.title: Dimensional Analysis Approach to Experiments in Z pinch Devices
arxiv-2601-12692.creator: Miguel Cárdenas
arxiv-2601-12692.description: Abstract The physical behavior of discharges in Z pinch devices can be completely deciphered in terms of only three dimensionless parameters. These parameters can be arranged in a way that draw a surface in 3 ​ D 3D space. This surface compiles all the accessible information on the macroscopic physical behavior of each possible Z pinch discharge.

pmc-11506069.title: Feature Contributions and Predictive Accuracy in Modeling Adolescent Daytime Sleepiness Using Machine Learning: The MeLiSA Study
pmc-11506069.creator: Mohammed A Mamun, Jannatul Mawa Misti, Md Emran Hasan, Firoj Al-Mamun, Moneerah Mohammad ALmerab, Johurul Islam, Mohammad Muhit, David Gozal, Anne M Fink
pmc-11506069.description: Background: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) among adolescents poses significant risks to academic performance, mental health, and overall well-being. This study examines the prevalence and risk factors of EDS in adolescents in Bangladesh and utilizes machine learning approaches to predict the risk of EDS. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1496 adolescents using a structured questionnaire.

pmc-11640170.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KABP051: Stability in Fruit Juices and Production of Bioactive Compounds During Their Fermentation
pmc-11640170.creator: Francesca Rizzi, Bibiana Juan, Jordi Espadaler-Mazo, Marta Capellas, Pol Huedo
pmc-11640170.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The lactic fermentation of fruit and vegetable juices by well-characterised probiotics remains relatively underexplored. We have investigated the stability and impact of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KABP051 fermentation on orange, apple, and peach juices by microbiological, physicochemical, and sensory evaluation means.

pmc-11675800.title: Relationship Between Psychological Factors and Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients with Chronic Low Back Pain
pmc-11675800.creator: Iva Dimitrijević, Dijana Hnatešen, Ivan Radoš, Dino Budrovac, Marija Raguž
pmc-11675800.description: Background: Low back pain has frequently been mentioned as the most common sort of chronic pain, and numerous studies have confirmed its influence on the health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Despite a great deal of research demonstrating the important part that psychological factors play in explaining HRQoL, a therapeutic setting that prioritizes the physical domain still predominates.

pmc-11728504.title: Awareness and Knowledge of Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals Among Pregnant Women and New Mothers: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study
pmc-11728504.creator: Esin Okman, Sıddika Songül Yalçın
pmc-11728504.description: Background/Objectives: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are exogenous substances that interfere with hormone regulation, leading to adverse health outcomes. Despite the wide use of EDCs in daily products like plastics, personal care items, and food packaging, public awareness remains low. Pregnant women and new mothers are particularly vulnerable, as exposure to EDCs during early life stages can have long-term health impacts.

pmc-12462456.title: Symmetry-broken MoS2 nanotubes through sequential sulfurization of MoO2 nanowires
pmc-12462456.creator: Lei Luo, Yao Wu, Lei Li, Zhonghan Zhang, Lu Zheng, Chao Zhu, Manzhang Xu, Weiwei Li, Ruihuan Duan, Yanchao He, Xin Zhou, Qundong Fu, Gang Wu, Jiefu Yang, Qi Wu, Wei Huang, Xuewen Wang, Zheng Liu
pmc-12462456.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanotubes are emerging quantum materials with distinctive symmetry-breaking properties, offering significant potential for energy conversion technologies. However, the direct synthesis of crystalline MoS2 nanotubes remains challenging due to limited understanding of their high-temperature growth mechanisms. Here, we present a robust and controllable strategy for the direct growth of crystalline MoS2 nanotubes with well-defined tubular morphology and high structural uniformity.

pmc-12720617.title: Impact of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with traditional Chinese Tuina for stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12720617.creator: Haihua Xie, Bo Huang, Jia Jiang, Sihui Cao, Dejun Wang, Liang Zhang, Liang Peng, Mi Liu
pmc-12720617.description: BackgroundStroke has emerged as one of the leading causes of long-term disability worldwide. Although the therapeutic effects of traditional Chinese Tuina and rTMS as monotherapies have been partially established, research on their combined application in stroke rehabilitation remains limited. This meta-analysis aims to investigate the effects of traditional Chinese Tuina combined with rTMS for stroke.

pmc-12832097.title: Characteristics of Traumatic Lower Extremity Amputation: Medical and Social Comorbidities
pmc-12832097.creator: Mark D Marino, Sophia Izhar, Heidi Israel, Patrickson Jean, John T Watson
pmc-12832097.description: BackgroundTraumatic amputations are life-altering injuries that remain prevalent despite the best efforts of physicians. While a multitude of research demonstrates various medical comorbidities that contribute to amputations, little attention has been paid to specific factors linked to traumatic amputation, even though trauma is the second most common etiology of amputation.

pmc-12953060.title: Therapeutic targeting of MALT1 in oncology: Mechanism, inhibitor development, and clinical prospects
pmc-12953060.creator: Xintao Cao, Peixia Wang, Yuan Ji, Yongliang Sun, Dejiu Zhang
pmc-12953060.description: MALT1, a multifunctional protease molecule, plays a pivotal role in the adaptive immunity by regulating immune cell survival, proliferation and activation through the nuclear transcription factor‐κB (NF‐κB) signaling pathway by scaffold and protease activities. Aberrant activation of MALT1 is implicated in the pathogenesis of hematologic malignancies, particularly diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma, and select solid tumors.

pmc-13064213.title: Implementing a multi-centric cohort study during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in a resource-constrained setting: challenges, adaptive solutions, and lessons from Brazil
pmc-13064213.creator: Lorena Guadalupe Barberia, Manuela de Almeida Roediger, Ricardo Queiroz Gurgel, Victor Santana Santos, Marcos de Carvalho Borges, Gustavo Adolfo Sierra Romero, Allex Jardim da Fonseca, Mauro Martins Teixeira, Mauricio Lacerda Nogueira, Cor Jesus Fernandes Fontes, Ivo Castelo Branco Coelho, Dhelio Ba
pmc-13064213.description: BackgroundConducting multicenter, longitudinal epidemiological studies on emerging pathogens in real time during health emergencies presents significant challenges, especially in low- and middle-income countries, where substantial logistical and resource constraints hinder the rapid design and implementation of research protocols. This is particularly difficult when the disease spreads rapidly and its nature changes due to the onset of vaccination.

pmc-13383130.title: Digital health risks and well-being: internet addiction, fear of missing out, and life satisfaction in Lebanese adults
pmc-13383130.creator: Shams Al Khateeb, Khaled Azzam, Nour Bannout, Chaimaa Abou Yassin, Abir Ghosson, Fatima Soufan, Miriam Al Battal
pmc-13383130.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundExcessive internet use might be linked to Internet Addiction Disorder (IAD), which is negatively linked to all aspects of life, including physical, mental, and social well-being. Internet use can bring about the sense of fear of missing out (FOMO), which is a social anxiety where the individual feels they are being left out; thus, it is a motivation to use the internet even more.

pmc-13573629.title: UBE2D4 Upregulation Promotes Cuproptosis Sensitivity in Colorectal Cancer
pmc-13573629.creator: Biaoyu Wang, Chan Li, Xianwen Guo, Zhihai Liang
pmc-13573629.description: BackgroundCuproptosis, a copper‐dependent form of regulated cell death, represents a potential therapeutic vulnerability in colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the regulatory mechanisms governing cuproptosis in CRC remain largely unknown.MethodsUBE2D4 expression was analyzed in the TCGA‐COAD cohort and validated in CRC cell lines (HCT116, HT29) and normal colon epithelial cells (FHC) by qRT‐PCR and western blot.

pmc-13627423.title: Pivoting in the pandemic: how HIV-focused community-health workers addressed COVID-19 disparities
pmc-13627423.creator: Sonjia Kenya, BreAnne Young, Olveen Carrasquillo
pmc-13627423.description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic significantly overburdened the U.S. healthcare system and magnified pre-existing care delivery gaps in communities of color. In Miami-Dade County, Black residents account for 64% of AIDS-related deaths and experienced a COVID-19 mortality rate of 6.1%, compared to 3.9% among White residents.

pmc-13634881.title: Data-Driven Clustering of Secretory Bone and Inflammatory Markers to Subphenotype Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis
pmc-13634881.creator: Simon Aberger, Ameen Abu-Hanna, Vianda Stel, Nicholas Chesnaye, Emanuel Zitt, Daniel Cejka, Thomas B. Dschietzig, Franz P. Armbruster, Hildegard Hafner-Gießauf, Maximilian Waller, Corinna Schabhüttl, Alexander H. Kirsch, Alexander R. Rosenkranz, Kathrin Eller
pmc-13634881.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionParathyroid hormone (PTH) remains the primary biomarker used to classify and monitor chronic kidney disease–mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD); nonetheless, its reliability for risk stratification and treatment guidance is limited. Multidimensional biomarker clustering that integrates indicators of bone turnover, vascular calcification, inflammatory and oxidative stress may better capture the heterogeneity of clinical phenotypes, improve risk stratification, and inform on new therapeutic approaches in dialysis care.MethodsWe conducted a computational analysis of a multicentric cohort study including 471 patients undergoing hemodialysis.
